From the EXP-66 discussion, 2026-11-14. Jack Heart: "I don't think we can make OpenRouter directly give us the exact API we want. The inference server for an LM is actually going to need a local process that itself calls ... OpenRouter and then I don't really think an inference server for Qwen is really any different than an inference server for the non-LLM models". So both fit EXP-73's InferenceServer(serve=...): a hosted model is a serve that runs a local proxy; a self-hosted one is a serve that starts the model server (Manabot has manabot/llm/vllm_runtime.py). Thorns to design for. Hosted: the API key must reach the machine without entering job records, identity or logs; no checkpoint, so a player's identity is a model name that can change underneath it; non-determinism; cost is per token and invisible to Etude's rental dollar limits; rate limits and seconds-long latency against game time limits; API errors must be infrastructure failures, not forfeits; tests cannot reach the network. Self-hosted: weights are tens of GB from outside Etude's checkpoints, delivered and verified inside the rental window; minutes of start-up; one LLM can fill the GPU, so servers cannot always share a machine. Both: a match can seat an LLM against a checkpoint policy, so one eval job needs more than one server (EXP-73 is told to allow that).
